R93.summary: Friends of the French crown ask the Pope to use his offices with the Emperor for a marriage of one of the Emperor's daughters to the King of France; the Pope will not move without knowing Philip II's mind, and the nuncio is to sound it discreetly and report.
R93.en:
Same holes as R93reading.md. Modern spelling; codes as names.

His Holiness is asked here by some friends of the crown of France to use his good offices with the Emperor so that he
be pleased to give one of his daughters as wife to the King of France; His Holiness has not wished to set this
negotiation moving without knowing the King's mind in this matter. Your Lordship will therefore find it out in the
way that seems most suitable and fitting to you, assuring him that His Holiness will never say a word of it before he
knows what his intention is, expressly; and once you have learned it […], you will let me know at the first
opportunity.

R94.summary: Covering letter Rome 7 Nov 1567 ("Con questa un poco di cifra"): the Pope does not mean to revoke the King's ancient privileges but to remove abuses grown through his ministers; the nuncio is to say so at a suitable moment, once the King is out of the trouble of the funerals; if the King strips the Holy See of its authority, the Pope will resist with spiritual arms "usque ad effusionem sanguinis".
R94.en:
Taking a good occasion, and invited also by the talk His Majesty sometimes has with Your Lordship on these matters of
jurisdiction, His Holiness wishes you to tell him freely that His Holiness does not intend to revoke his ancient
privileges, but rather to remove the abuses that have grown up in them through the fault of his ministers, who, for
their own private interest more than for anything else, have tried to enlarge them and to use them to the detriment
of that authority which granted His Majesty's predecessors the graces and privileges they allege. But this will have
to be said at a suitable moment, as I tell you, […] His Majesty begins […] freely, and is out of the trouble of the
funerals;

R95.summary: The French ambassador's claim about raising troops in the State of Milan would give the King cause to withdraw his protection; the crusade alms: the Pope acted so that Christian discipline should not slacken in Spain, not to deny the indulgence, and will grant a new concession; he grieves more for the King's soul than for any human respect; the nuncio is to speak in this sense.
R95.en:
Answering your letters of last month more particularly, I tell you that, were what the French Ambassador has said not
true — about being able to raise troops in the State of Milan in case it were attacked from here — it would give the
King just cause to give up his protection and even to become indignant with that Ambassador, who spreads such
falsehoods. Now as to the [08.: the Crusade?], His Holiness did not say it […] so that those who gave the alms should
not gain the indulgence, but so that Christian discipline should not slacken in Spain, as has happened elsewhere; but
His Holiness is content to grant him a new concession of it in such manner as his conscience allows, at the great
instance made [an] by […], who in the office he [?performed] on this matter did not fail to say that the King would
become estranged from this Holy See;

R96.summary: Rome, 19 May 1568: the Pope awaits the answer on the Emperor-King of France marriage (hoping for a league of the three chief princes); Scipione [?Cuttinardo], charged as a heretic by the Holy Office, aspires to be Regent of the Collateral in Naples - the King to be told at once; difficulties over the order against the Jeronimites to be reported.
R96.en:
Same holes as R96reading.md. Modern spelling; codes as names.

His Holiness waits to hear some answer from Your Lordship on the particular of the marriage between the Emperor and
the King of France, about which I wrote to you in the last few days so that you might learn the Emperor's view of it,
His Holiness judging that if by chance it were concluded, one could easily hope for some good union or league among
these three chief princes of Christendom. You will let the King know as soon as possible that in this Holy Office
Scipione [?Cuttinardo] has been charged as a heretic, who, it is understood here, aspires to be Regent of the
Collateral [Council of Naples]; and as the news is of great importance, as you see, do not fail to tell it to the
King at once in His Holiness's name.

R97.summary: The Duke of Ferrara, displeased over the Bolognese exiles (Cavaliere Gualengo), may complain to the King through Count Ercole Tassone; the Pope's case under the investiture. The French ambassador in Constantinople offers to join Huguenots and Protestants with the Turks; in Adrianople he urged Piali Pasha to bring the fleet against Rome; his removal is to be sought.
R97.en:
Same holes as R97reading.md. Modern spelling; codes as names.

It is known for certain that the Duke of Ferrara, out of the dissatisfaction he has perhaps felt with His Holiness in
a matter of the exiles of the county of Bologna, dealt with here in his name by the Cavaliere Gualengo, intends to
make some complaint of it to the King; and if Count Ercole Tassone comes to your court he will probably have a
particular commission to speak to him on this matter. That office ought not to be done by this ambassador,
considering the fatherly affection His Holiness bears him and the little respect shown on his side to this Holy See,
of which he is a feudatary, not observing the terms of his investiture, and in particular one that obliges him to
hand over the exiles of this state whenever they are asked of him.

R98.summary: The King's orders to his ministers in Italy against a Huguenot move into Italy are good, but ministers delay waiting for new commissions; the nuncio is to press for express orders now, so that the Pope can call on them in time for the security of Italy.
R98.en:
Same holes as R98reading.md. Modern spelling; codes as names.

Although the orders which the King wrote in recent days that he had sent to his ministers in Italy, so that they
should be provided in case the Huguenots of France wished to turn towards these parts, were good and suited to the
need, nevertheless, because such provisions are often delayed by the ministers themselves wanting to wait for new
commissions from the King and new limited orders, whereby harm is done or at least the enterprise is put off while
these commissions are awaited, Your Lordship will therefore press His Majesty to give express and limited orders to
his ministers in Italy now, so that if the case should ever come — which God forbid — His Holiness [?could] make use
of them in time and place, for the public good [?and] for the security of Italy and of His Majesty's states […].

R99.summary: The Pope's plan for two galleys of the Order of St Lazarus (sought from Gian Andrea Doria) opposed by Don John of Austria, whom the Pope answered sharply; in Milan the Senate threatened the archbishop's vicar over the armed household at the Corpus Domini procession, and the Pope will use spiritual arms.
R99.en:
Same holes as R99reading.md. Modern spelling; codes as names.

And His Holiness has resolved to make trial of this order of St Lazarus, and had instructed the Grand Master to
provide himself with two galleys [?so that] he could keep to these seas and run them for the safety of navigators;
and he already hoped to have found them from Signor Gian Andrea Doria, [2020] […] His Holiness […] this; Don John has
made [?a little] noise about it with His Holiness, opposing in this the plan of the said Grand Master [?and] chiefly
His Holiness's will, and the matter has not passed without some ill feeling.

R100.summary: The King's ministers mean to deceive the nuncio over the Inquisition of Catalonia and keep people from coming to him for absolution; the ambassador presses for the case to be referred to the King; without waiting for another resolution the nuncio is to execute the brief when the parties ask.
R100.en:
From the way His Majesty's ministers proceed one can see that they intend to deceive Your Lordship in that matter of
the Inquisition of Catalonia, and they prevent those people from coming to you for absolution. Here the Ambassador is
now pressing His Holiness that this case be referred to His Majesty in Spain; so, without waiting for any resolution
from here other than the first, Your Lordship is to put the brief into execution when the parties ask you for it.

R101.summary: The Pope accepted the hackney and the St Peter's day dues with the fisc's protest, not as census but as fruits of a fief of the Holy See, and claims devolution under the investitures of Julius II and Julius III; the King's ministers have raised a schism in Naples, imprisoning the bishops' notaries and executors (an aged doctor died in prison); God will punish who troubles His Church, and the Pope will have to take measures if the King does not remedy it.
R101.en:
For Your Lordship's instruction, [you will know?] that His Holiness [recently?] accepted the hackney and the customary
moneys paid on St Peter's day, but with a protest by the fisc, to which His Holiness adheres — that is, that he has
not accepted it as a census but as the fruits of that kingdom, a direct fief of this Holy See — and claims the
devolution [of the kingdom] on many heads of the investiture of Julius II and Julius III, of holy memory. The
King or his ministers having by his order stirred up a manifest schism in that kingdom, as anyone free of passion can
make out, taking away obedience to the Apostolic See, so that neither the bishops nor their vicars can have notaries
to serve them, nor executors who, for the most part, in doing their office are not imprisoned by the royal ministers;
and […] from this […] a doctor from [?Sora], of decrepit age, was left to die in prison.

R102.summary: Summer 1569: the Pope thinks Cardinal Espinosa fails in his duty towards the Holy See at Philip II's court and has said he regrets making him cardinal; the nuncio may let him know if amendment can be hoped for.
R102.en:
Same holes as R102reading.md. Modern spelling; codes as names.

In the public letter I have written more mildly of Cardinal [Espinosa] than His Holiness has in truth spoken of him
and of his bad conduct; but I want you to know, for your own information, that His Holiness ordered me to let Your
Lordship know that the Cardinal fails in many things to do the office he should with the King in the service of this
Holy See, so that His Holiness has judged him unworthy of the dignity he holds, and has said at times that he [?did
not] regret having made him cardinal. But if one could hope for amendment in him, it would be well to let him know it;
but in this Your Lordship will act as you think fits the time and the persons, leaving it to your [?own] prudence.

R115.summary: Two months after asking (30 November) for the royal nomination of Francisco de Reinoso, the Pope's scalco, to the see of Monreale, with the transfer of the pensions on the archdeaconry of Toledo, the nuncio is to press Philip II for a speedy dispatch.
R115.en:
Same holes as R115reading.md. Modern spelling; codes as names.

I wrote to [4050] [?of Alessandrino] two months ago, on the last day of November, that he should ask the King in His
Holiness's name for the nomination to the church of Monreale in the person of Don [?Francisco] de Reinoso, private
steward of [2010], and also the consent to be able to transfer the pensions that he had laid on the archdeaconry of
Toledo onto the same church, informing me [?also] of the truth […]; of […] that, as I have had no [9070] so far, His
Holiness wished me to give Your Lordship the same commission, so that you do not fail to speak of it with the King
[…] first you can have a good occasion, pressing him for the speedy dispatch, so that the matter does not drag on
for ever, and then to let me know […] his decision.
